Read an export of the sheepdog package

Source: R/fp_read_sheepdog.R
fp_read_sheepdog.Rd

Reads the folder written by sheepdog::export_occupancy_data(), which follows the sheepdog-occupancy schema (version 1.x): every occasion of a passive acoustic survey, the classifier predictions, the reviewed clips with their sampling design, and the recordings annotated by ear. The tables come back in the forms that fp_aggregate() and fp_data() expect.

Usage

fp_read_sheepdog(path, species = NULL, keep_top = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Folder of the export, holding schema.json.

species

Optional species to keep, matched against species_code (the classifier label, such as "Nyctidromus albicollis_Common Pauraque") and species (the short code that sheepdog derives from it). Without it, an export of several species is kept whole, and the verdicts and annotated recordings of all species are mixed: name the target species.

keep_top

Keep reviewed clips drawn with sampling_mode = "top"? See Details.

Value

A list of class fp_sheepdog with the data frames occasions (site, occasion_id, source_audio, recording_date, recording_hour, night, start, duration, then any occasion covariates), detections (one row per prediction: site, occasion_id, species_code, species, start, confidence), scores (highest score and number of predictions per occasion and species), validation (one row per reviewed clip, with start, end, confidence, sampling_mode, inclusion_prob, verdict as TRUE, FALSE or NA), verified (one row per annotated recording, with y, 1 or 0, and inclusion_prob), sites, the parsed schema, and files (paths of the tables found). Tables absent from the export are NULL.

Details

Which reviewed clips. The false-positive models of crywolf treat the checked detections as chosen independently of the classifier's score. Clips of the "random_detections" design are; clips of the "top" design, the highest-scoring detections, are not: they hold fewer false positives than a random sample and would make the false-positive rate look lower than it is. By default they are dropped with a warning (keep_top = FALSE); they remain useful to calibrate the classifier within sheepdog.

Clips and recordings. A positive clip proves that the species called in its occasion; a negative clip says only that this prediction was false. These go to validation, for the observation-confirmation design through fp_aggregate(validation = ). A recording annotated by ear ("random_recordings") gives the state of the whole occasion; these go to verified, the verified method of fp_data().

Censored scores. Only predictions with a confidence of at least schema$min_confidence were exported, so thresholds below it count every exported prediction and no more.

Occasions are identified by site and occasion_id; pass by = c("site", "occasion_id") to fp_aggregate(). Identifiers, dates and the keys of the calibration (such as month) are read as text. The occasion covariates of the export (schema$occasion_covariates, from schema version 1.1) are extra columns of occasions. The calibration draws (calibration_draws.parquet) and the detection histories sheepdog drew from them (occasion_draws.parquet, schema 1.2), when present, are not read here; their path is in files. When the calibration has continuous covariates (schema$calibration$covariates, schema 1.3), the export holds only the histories sheepdog drew, and no calibration draws.

See also

fp_aggregate(), fp_data(), fp_read_validation()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# the tables hold only the target species, so fp_aggregate() needs no
# `species`
x <- fp_read_sheepdog("occupancy_export", species = "compau")
auto <- fp_aggregate(x$occasions, x$detections, threshold = 0.5,
                     by = c("site", "occasion_id"), validation = x$validation)
d <- fp_data(auto, x$sites, x$verified, confirmed = c("n_true", "n_false"))
} # }
